socket.summary: Creates an endpoint for network communication and returns a file descriptor for it.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.meaning: address family (e.g. AF_INET = IPv4, AF_INET6 = IPv6, AF_UNIX = local socket)

parameters.name: type
parameters.meaning: socket type (e.g. SOCK_STREAM = reliable connection-oriented/TCP, SOCK_DGRAM = connectionless/UDP)

parameters.name: protocol
parameters.meaning: specific protocol (0 = the default protocol for the given domain/type)

return.meaning: a file descriptor for the new socket on success

setsockopt.summary: Sets a configuration option on a socket.

parameters.name: level
parameters.meaning: the option's protocol level (e.g. SOL_SOCKET = socket-API-level options)

parameters.name: optname
parameters.meaning: which option to set (e.g. SO_REUSEADDR = allow rebinding an address still in TIME_WAIT)

parameters.name: optval
parameters.meaning: pointer to the value to set the option to

parameters.name: optlen
parameters.meaning: size in bytes of the value pointed to by optval

rules.meaning: setting the option failed (see errno) - the call's effect did NOT take place

bind.summary: Assigns a local address (IP + port) to a socket.

parameters.name: addr
parameters.meaning: the local address (IP and port) to bind the socket to

parameters.name: addrlen
parameters.meaning: size in bytes of the addr structure

rules.meaning: the bind failed (see errno - commonly EADDRINUSE, the port is already in use)
the address was successfully bound to the socket

listen.summary: Marks a bound socket as passive/listening, ready to accept incoming connections.

parameters.name: sockfd
parameters.meaning: the bound socket to start listening on

parameters.name: backlog
parameters.meaning: maximum number of pending (not-yet-accepted) connections to queue

rules.meaning: the socket could not be put into listening state (see errno)
the socket is now listening for incoming connections

accept.summary: Blocks until a client connects to a listening socket, then returns a NEW socket connected to that client.

parameters.name: sockfd
parameters.meaning: the listening socket to accept a connection from

parameters.name: addr
parameters.meaning: (output) filled in with the connecting client's address

parameters.name: addrlen
parameters.meaning: (input/output) size of the addr buffer on input, actual address size written on output

return.meaning: a NEW file descriptor for the accepted connection on success (the original sockfd keeps listening)

rules.meaning: no connection was accepted - an error occurred (see errno)
a new connected-client socket file descriptor

recv.summary: Reads up to `len` bytes from an already-connected socket into `buf`.

parameters.name: sockfd
parameters.meaning: the connected socket to read from

parameters.name: buf
parameters.meaning: destination buffer that receives the incoming bytes

parameters.name: len
parameters.meaning: maximum number of bytes to read into buf

parameters.name: flags
parameters.meaning: receive behavior flags (0 = normal blocking receive)

return.meaning: the number of bytes actually placed into buf

rules.meaning: a receive error occurred (see errno) - no data was read
the peer performed an orderly shutdown - the connection is closed, no more data will ever arrive
the number of bytes of real data successfully received into buf

send.summary: Writes up to `len` bytes from `buf` to an already-connected socket.

parameters.name: sockfd
parameters.meaning: the connected socket to write to

parameters.name: buf
parameters.meaning: source buffer containing the bytes to send

parameters.name: len
parameters.meaning: number of bytes from buf to send

parameters.name: flags
parameters.meaning: send behavior flags (0 = normal blocking send)

return.meaning: the number of bytes actually queued/sent

rules.meaning: a send error occurred (see errno) - no data was sent
the number of bytes successfully sent (may be less than len)

htons.summary: Converts a 16-bit value from host byte order to network byte order (big-endian) - used to prepare a port number for a sockaddr_in.

parameters.name: hostshort
parameters.meaning: the 16-bit value in the host's native byte order

return.meaning: the same value, reordered into network byte order - there is no error case

perror.summary: Writes a human-readable description of the CURRENT errno value to standard error (stderr), prefixed by the caller's own message.

parameters.name: s
parameters.meaning: a caller-supplied prefix string (e.g. the name of the call that just failed) prepended to the error text

return.meaning: none (void) - always writes to stderr, never fails observably

printf.summary: Formats and writes text to standard output (stdout).

return.meaning: the number of characters written on success, or a negative value if an output error occurred

malloc.summary: Allocates a block of uninitialized heap memory.

return.meaning: a pointer to the allocated block on success

rules.meaning: allocation failed (out of memory) - the pointer is NULL, must not be dereferenced
a valid pointer to size bytes of uninitialized heap memory

free.summary: Releases a block of heap memory previously returned by malloc/calloc/realloc, making it invalid to use afterward.

parameters.name: ptr
parameters.meaning: the pointer to release (freeing NULL is explicitly a safe no-op)

memset.summary: Fills a block of memory with a constant byte value.

parameters.name: s
parameters.meaning: start of the memory region to fill

parameters.name: c
parameters.meaning: the byte value to write into every position (commonly 0, to zero-initialize)

return.meaning: returns s unchanged (rarely used, since the caller already has s)

memcpy.summary: Copies a block of memory from one location to another (regions must not overlap).

parameters.name: dest
parameters.meaning: destination address the bytes are copied INTO

parameters.name: src
parameters.meaning: source address the bytes are copied FROM

return.meaning: returns dest unchanged (rarely used, since the caller already has dest)

open.summary: Opens (or creates) a file/device special file, returning a file descriptor for it.

parameters.name: pathname
parameters.meaning: path of the file/device to open

parameters.name: flags
parameters.meaning: access mode and behavior flags (e.g. O_RDWR = read+write, O_SYNC = writes complete before returning)

parameters.name: mode
parameters.meaning: permission bits to apply if the file is being newly created (only used with O_CREAT)

rules.meaning: the file/device could not be opened (see errno - permissions, doesn't exist, etc.)

close.summary: Closes a file descriptor, releasing the underlying resource.

rules.meaning: the close failed (see errno) - rare, but means the fd's state is now unspecified

mmap.summary: Maps a region of a file/device directly into this process's virtual address space, so ordinary memory reads/writes act on the underlying file/device.

parameters.name: addr
parameters.meaning: preferred starting address (NULL = let the kernel choose the address)

parameters.name: prot
parameters.meaning: memory protection for the mapping (e.g. PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE = readable and writable)

parameters.name: flags
parameters.meaning: mapping visibility (e.g. MAP_SHARED = writes go through to the underlying file/device and are visible to other mappers; MAP_PRIVATE = copy-on-write, changes stay local)

parameters.name: fd
parameters.meaning: file descriptor of the already-open file/device being mapped

parameters.name: offset
parameters.meaning: byte offset within the file/device where the mapping begins (for /dev/mem, this IS the physical address being mapped)

return.meaning: a pointer usable to directly read/write the mapped region on success

rules.meaning: the mapping failed (see errno) - the pointer must NOT be dereferenced or passed to munmap

munmap.summary: Unmaps a memory region previously established by mmap, releasing that virtual address range - the mapped file/device is untouched, only this process's access to it via that pointer is removed.

parameters.name: addr
parameters.meaning: starting address of the mapping to remove (must be a value previously returned by mmap)

parameters.name: length
parameters.meaning: size of the region to unmap (should match the original mmap length)

pthread_create.summary: Creates a new thread that begins executing the given start-routine function, running concurrently with the caller.

parameters.name: thread
parameters.meaning: (output) filled in with an identifier for the newly created thread

parameters.name: start_routine
parameters.meaning: the function the new thread begins executing

parameters.name: arg
parameters.meaning: the single argument passed through to start_routine when the new thread begins

return.meaning: 0 on success - NOTE this returns a raw error NUMBER directly, NOT via errno like most other calls here

rules.meaning: the thread was created and is now running concurrently
thread creation failed - the returned value IS the error number (not read from errno)

pthread_detach.summary: Marks a thread as detached, so its resources are automatically released when it exits (no other thread needs to pthread_join it).

parameters.name: thread
parameters.meaning: identifier of the thread to detach

rules.meaning: detaching failed - the returned value is the error number

exit.summary: Immediately terminates the calling PROCESS (not just the current function) - does not return.

parameters.name: status
parameters.meaning: the process exit status reported to the parent process/shell (0 = conventionally success, nonzero = failure)

read.summary: Reads up to count bytes from a file descriptor into a buffer.

parameters.name: fd
parameters.meaning: the open file descriptor to read from

parameters.name: count
parameters.meaning: maximum number of bytes to read

return.meaning: the number of bytes actually read

rules.meaning: end of file (or the peer closed the connection) - no more data
that many bytes of real data were read

write.summary: Writes up to count bytes from a buffer to a file descriptor.

parameters.name: fd
parameters.meaning: the open file descriptor to write to

return.meaning: the number of bytes actually written (can be fewer than count)

rules.meaning: that many bytes were written - a short write needs the caller to retry the rest

pread.summary: Reads or writes at an explicit file offset without moving the file position.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.meaning: byte offset in the file at which to start

pwrite.summary: Reads or writes at an explicit file offset without moving the file position.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.meaning: byte offset in the file at which to start

lseek.summary: Moves the read/write position of an open file.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.meaning: byte distance to move, interpreted according to whence

parameters.name: whence
parameters.meaning: the reference point (SEEK_SET = file start, SEEK_CUR = current position, SEEK_END = file end)

return.meaning: the new position measured from the start of the file

fsync.summary: Forces buffered changes of a file to be physically written to the storage device.

parameters.name: fd
parameters.meaning: the open file descriptor to flush

rules.meaning: data is durably on the device

fdatasync.summary: Forces buffered changes of a file to be physically written to the storage device.

parameters.name: fd
parameters.meaning: the open file descriptor to flush

rules.meaning: data is durably on the device

dup.summary: Duplicates a file descriptor so two numbers refer to the same open file.

parameters.name: newfd
parameters.meaning: the descriptor number to make into a copy (dup2 closes it first if it is open)

dup2.summary: Duplicates a file descriptor so two numbers refer to the same open file.

parameters.name: newfd
parameters.meaning: the descriptor number to make into a copy (dup2 closes it first if it is open)

fcntl.summary: Performs a control operation on a file descriptor (flags, locks, duplicate).

parameters.name: cmd
parameters.meaning: which operation to perform (F_GETFL, F_SETFL, F_SETFD, F_DUPFD, F_SETLK ...)

ioctl.summary: Sends a device-specific control request to a file descriptor (driver).

parameters.name: argp
parameters.meaning: pointer to the request's argument/result data

rules.meaning: the request failed or is unsupported (see errno)

stat.summary: Reads file metadata (size, type, permissions, timestamps) into a struct stat.

parameters.name: path
parameters.meaning: path of the file (fstat takes an open descriptor instead)

parameters.name: buf
parameters.meaning: the struct stat that receives the metadata

rules.meaning: the metadata could not be read (see errno - missing file, permissions)

lstat.summary: Reads file metadata (size, type, permissions, timestamps) into a struct stat.

parameters.name: path
parameters.meaning: path of the file (fstat takes an open descriptor instead)

parameters.name: buf
parameters.meaning: the struct stat that receives the metadata

rules.meaning: the metadata could not be read (see errno - missing file, permissions)

fstat.summary: Reads file metadata (size, type, permissions, timestamps) into a struct stat.

parameters.meaning: path of the file (fstat takes an open descriptor instead)

parameters.name: buf
parameters.meaning: the struct stat that receives the metadata

rules.meaning: the metadata could not be read (see errno - missing file, permissions)

access.summary: Checks whether the calling process may access a path in the given way.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.meaning: what to check (F_OK = exists, R_OK = readable, W_OK = writable, X_OK = executable)

rules.meaning: not allowed or does not exist (see errno)

chmod.summary: Changes the permission bits of a file.

fchmod.summary: Changes the permission bits of a file.

unlink.summary: Deletes a file name (and the file once no links or open handles remain).

parameters.name: pathname
parameters.meaning: path of the file to delete

remove.summary: Deletes a file name (and the file once no links or open handles remain).

parameters.name: pathname
parameters.meaning: path of the file to delete

rename.summary: Renames or moves a file or directory (atomic within one filesystem).

parameters.name: newpath
parameters.meaning: new path (an existing target is replaced)

rules.meaning: the rename failed (see errno - e.g. cross-device)

parameters.name: mode
parameters.meaning: permission bits for it (masked by umask)

rules.meaning: creation failed (see errno - already exists, no permission)
removal failed (see errno - not empty, missing)

opendir.summary: Opens a directory for listing its entries.

rules.meaning: could not open the directory (see errno)

readdir.summary: Returns the next entry of an open directory.

return.meaning: a pointer to the next entry, or NULL at the end

rules.meaning: no more entries (or an error - check errno)

fopen.summary: Opens a file as a buffered stream (FILE*).

parameters.name: mode
parameters.meaning: open mode ("r" read, "w" truncate+write, "a" append, plus "b" binary and "+" update)

return.meaning: a FILE stream, or NULL on failure

rules.meaning: could not open the file (see errno)

fclose.summary: Flushes and closes a buffered stream.

rules.meaning: closing failed (buffered data may be lost)

fread.summary: Reads up to nmemb items of size bytes from a stream.

parameters.name: size
parameters.meaning: size in bytes of each item

return.meaning: the number of whole items read

rules.meaning: nothing read - end of file or an error (use feof/ferror)
that many items were read (fewer than nmemb means EOF or error)

fwrite.summary: Writes nmemb items of size bytes to a stream.

parameters.name: size
parameters.meaning: size in bytes of each item

return.meaning: the number of whole items written

rules.meaning: that many items were written (fewer than nmemb means a write error)

fgets.summary: Reads one line (at most size-1 characters) from a stream into a buffer.

parameters.name: size
parameters.meaning: buffer capacity including the terminating NUL

return.meaning: s on success, NULL at EOF or on error

rules.meaning: end of file or read error - buffer contents are unusable
a line was read into s

fputs.summary: Writes a string to a stream (puts to stdout, adding a newline).

return.meaning: a non-negative number on success, EOF on error

puts.summary: Writes a string to a stream (puts to stdout, adding a newline).

return.meaning: a non-negative number on success, EOF on error

fflush.summary: Writes any buffered output of a stream to its destination.

parameters.name: stream
parameters.meaning: the FILE* to flush (NULL flushes all output streams)

fseek.summary: Moves the position of a stream.

ftell.summary: Returns the current position of a stream.

return.meaning: the position in bytes from the start, or -1 on error

sprintf.summary: Formats text into a buffer (snprintf bounds the output to size bytes).

snprintf.summary: Formats text into a buffer (snprintf bounds the output to size bytes).

strncat.summary: Appends a string to the end of another string.

strncmp.summary: Compares two strings or memory blocks byte by byte.

memcmp.summary: Compares two strings or memory blocks byte by byte.

document.getElementById.summary: Looks up a single element in the document by its exact `id` attribute.

parameters.name: id
parameters.meaning: the exact `id` attribute value to look up (no `#` prefix, unlike a CSS selector)

return.meaning: the matching Element, or null if no element has that id

rules.meaning: no element with that id exists in the document right now

document.querySelector.summary: Looks up the FIRST element in the document matching a CSS selector.

parameters.name: selector
parameters.meaning: a CSS selector string (class/id/attribute/combinator - any valid CSS selector syntax)

return.meaning: the first matching Element, or null if nothing matches

rules.meaning: no element matches that selector right now

document.querySelectorAll.summary: Looks up EVERY element in the document matching a CSS selector.

return.meaning: a static NodeList of every matching element (empty if none match, never null)

document.createElement.summary: Creates a new, detached DOM element - not yet attached anywhere in the document until appended.

parameters.name: tagName
parameters.meaning: the HTML tag name to create (e.g. `div`, `button`, `img`)

document.createTextNode.summary: Creates a new, detached text node.

parameters.name: data
parameters.meaning: the literal text content of the node

return.meaning: the newly created, unattached Text node

addEventListener.summary: Registers a callback to run whenever the given event fires on {receiver}.

parameters.name: type
parameters.meaning: the event name to listen for (e.g. `click`, `submit`, `keydown`)

parameters.name: listener
parameters.meaning: the callback invoked with the Event object when it fires

parameters.name: options
parameters.meaning: optional flags (e.g. `{once: true}`, `{capture: true}`) or a boolean useCapture

removeEventListener.summary: Unregisters a previously-registered event listener from {receiver} (must be the SAME function reference used to add it).

parameters.name: type
parameters.meaning: the event name it was registered for

parameters.name: listener
parameters.meaning: the exact callback reference originally passed to addEventListener

parameters.name: options
parameters.meaning: must match the options used when adding it, or removal silently fails

dispatchEvent.summary: Manually fires an event on {receiver}, synchronously running every matching registered listener.

parameters.name: event
parameters.meaning: the Event (or CustomEvent) instance to dispatch

appendChild.summary: Attaches a node as the last child of {receiver}, moving it out of its previous parent if it had one.

removeChild.summary: Detaches a direct child node from {receiver}.

parameters.name: child
parameters.meaning: the direct child node to remove

setAttribute.summary: Sets an HTML attribute on {receiver} (creating it if absent, overwriting its value if present).

parameters.name: value
parameters.meaning: the attribute's new value (always coerced to a string)

getAttribute.summary: Reads the current value of an HTML attribute on {receiver}.

return.meaning: the attribute's string value, or null if the attribute isn't set

rules.meaning: the attribute isn't set on this element
the attribute is set, with this value

removeAttribute.summary: Removes an HTML attribute from {receiver} entirely.

closest.summary: Walks up from {receiver} through its own ancestors (starting with itself) for the nearest one matching a CSS selector.

parameters.name: selector
parameters.meaning: a CSS selector to match an ancestor (or this element itself) against

return.meaning: the nearest matching element (possibly this one itself), or null if none of its ancestors match

rules.meaning: neither this element nor any ancestor matches that selector
a matching ancestor (or this element itself) was found

matches.summary: Tests whether {receiver} itself matches a CSS selector, without touching the DOM tree at all.

parameters.name: selector
parameters.meaning: a CSS selector to test this element against

return.meaning: true if this element matches the selector, false otherwise

localStorage.getItem.summary: Reads a value from the browser's persistent localStorage (survives page reloads/browser restarts, scoped to this origin).

return.meaning: the stored string value, or null if that key was never set

rules.meaning: no value is stored under that key
a value was found under that key

localStorage.setItem.summary: Writes a value into the browser's persistent localStorage (survives page reloads/browser restarts, scoped to this origin).

parameters.name: key
parameters.meaning: the storage key to write under

parameters.name: value
parameters.meaning: the value to store (always coerced to a string - objects must be JSON.stringify'd first)

localStorage.removeItem.summary: Deletes one key from the browser's persistent localStorage.

fetch.summary: Starts an asynchronous HTTP request; the returned Promise resolves once RESPONSE HEADERS arrive (not once the body is fully read).

pop.summary: Removes and returns the last element of {receiver}, mutating it in place.

shift.summary: Removes and returns the first element of {receiver}, mutating it in place (every remaining element shifts down one index).

unshift.summary: Inserts one or more elements at the start of {receiver}, mutating it in place (every existing element shifts up).
